title: Voxel GI is extremely dark when used with "use physical light units"
body: ### Tested versions Reproducible in v4.6.3.stable.official [7d41c59c4] confirmed present in earlier versions ### System information Godot v4.6.3.stable - Fedora Linux 44 (KDE Plasma Desktop Edition) on Wayland - Wayland display driver, Single-window, 1 monitor - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3060 Laptop GPU - AMD Ryzen 9 5900HS with Radeon Graphics (16 threads) - 15.01 GiB memory ### Issue description Voxel GI cannot capture the range required to be effective with Godot in physical light units mode. This makes voxel GI unusable in a PBR project. Physical light units on Physical light units off (note: the intensity of the emissive material will be darker in physical light units but in testing it doesn't matter how bright emisive materials or light sources are, they will not contribute to voxel gi in any meaningful way under physical light mode) ### Steps to reproduce Open a or create a scene with Voxel GI using Physical Light Units in the project settings Global illumination will appear exremely dark ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) [voxel-gi-bug-report-nonphys.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/28649283/voxel-gi-bug-report-nonphys.zip) * Observe the state of voxel gi * Enable "use physical light units" in project settings and restart editor * Re-bake the voxel gi under physical lights (it wont make a difference) * It should be overly dark
